claims: C1 when a requested format conflicts with a higher-level instruction and the format offers a refusal mechanism, the assistant should use that mechanism
C2 when a requested format conflicts with a higher-level instruction and the format offers no refusal mechanism, the assistant should break the format and refuse in text

concepts.name: format_provides_refusal_mechanism
concepts.gloss: F is a requested output format that provides a built-in way for the assistant to refuse
concepts.inference: the node's claim distinguishes formats that provide a way to refuse from those that do not

concepts.name: format_conflicts_with_instruction
concepts.gloss: following format F would violate higher-level instruction I
concepts.inference: the source text says the assistant should refuse when following the format would violate a higher-level instruction; this relation captures that conflict

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from a level that outranks the instruction under evaluation
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the shared-name contract assigns; the source text refers to 'a higher-level instruction' without defining the ranking

asserts.read_back: when format % provides a way to refuse and following % would violate higher-level instruction %, the assistant should use that refusal mechanism
when format % provides no way to refuse and following % would violate higher-level instruction %, the assistant should break format and refuse in text

closure.reason: the clause states a preference for using the refusal mechanism when one exists; it does not forbid other conduct, so silence permits
the clause states a preference for breaking format and refusing in text when no refusal mechanism exists; it does not forbid other conduct, so silence permits
